description: Introduce sets as fundamental mathematical containers, show standard set notation, define elements and membership symbols, and present key properties and common ways to represent sets.
objectives: Understand the convenience of referencing objects by encapsulating them in sets.
Understand the notation for indicating whether an object is an element of a set.
Know the benefits and caveats associated with the three primary ways of declaring/representing sets.
Be able to convert sets from one form to another.
Be aware that sets can contain other sets.
prerequisites: These lecture notes are foundational and do not require any other foundational knowledge.
Students with knowledge of programming languages will likely find the encapsulating applications of sets more familiar.

content_list.title: Purpose of Mathematical sets
content_list.description: Motivate sets as mathematical containers for organizing and referencing objects, and introduce basic set notation and examples.

content_list.title: Set Elements
content_list.description: Define what set elements are and use symbolic mathematical notation to indicate whether an object is an element of a set.

content_list.title: Properties Of Sets
content_list.description: Explain the two core properties of sets: order does not matter and duplicates are not included.

content_list.title: Methods To Represent Sets
content_list.description: Compare sentence, roster, and set-builder representations, including when each is appropriate and how to read/write them.
